Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second essay. The Umpires are out and the Sri Lanka Under-19 fielders take their positions. Nathaniel Hlabangana and Ryan Kamwemba walk to bat for Zimbabwe Under-19. Garuka Sanketh has the new ball and is raring to go.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Considering the variable bounce on this pitch, Sri Lanka Under-19 would believe it to be a competitive total. Will Zimbabwe Under-19 successfully chase down this total, or will Sri Lanka's bowling lineup create challenges? Stay tuned for an exciting second innings unfolding shortly.

Kohl Eksteen is down for a chat. He says that the captain had a look at the pitch and told them there would be some movement off the pitch and they did exactly that. He then says that the target looks like a decent total and will back the batters to get them although the outfield doesn't seem to be very fast. He further says that they will look to utilize the powerplay and will look forward to starting off well. He then says that he is very excited and honoured to play for his country and play in front of this crowd.

Sri Lanka Under-19, on the other hand, would be immensely disappointed with the challenging start they encountered, losing their top three batters with just 12 runs on the board. The duo of Ravishan De Silva and Rusanda Gamage showcased resilience, weathering the storm of the new ball attack and stabilizing the innings with a crucial partnership of 54 runs before both players were eventually dismissed. The middle order, led by Sharujan Shanmuganathan and Dinura Kalupahana, initiated a counterattack and forged an impressive 80-run partnership that steered Sri Lanka back on track. Ruvishan Perera's cameo towards the end added valuable runs, pushing Sri Lanka's total to 204.

A sensational bowling effort from Zimbabwe Under-19 to bowl Sri Lanka Under-19 out for 204! After winning the toss and opting to bowl first, they got off to an ideal start with Kohl Eksteen making an early breakthrough in the very first over. Anesu Kamuriwo continued the momentum by claiming the wicket of Pulindu Perera. Sri Lanka's skipper, under Kohl Eksteen's bowling prowess, only had a brief stay at the crease. Despite a resilient partnership between Ravishan De Silva and Rusanda Gamage, Zimbabwe's bowlers managed to keep a lid on the scoring rate. Although there were a couple of missed opportunities in the field, Panashe Taruvinga's crucial breakthrough by knocking the stumps of Rusanda Gamage tilted the game back in Zimbabwe's favour. Ryan Simbi, following a tight spell, secured another pivotal wicket of the well-set batter Ravishan De Silva. A significant partnership of 80 runs between Sharujan Shanmuganathan and Dinura Kalupahana was then terminated by skipper Schonken, after which Zimbabwe ensured they tightened their grip on the match, not allowing Sri Lanka to escape with any further advantage. Newman Nyamhuri finished things off with two wickets restricting Sri Lanka to 204 runs.

Gets the ball to tail back into the batter, on middle, on a yorker length, Garuka Sanketh stays leg side of the ball as he tries to keep this one out. The ball rushes him and goes past the inside edge to clatter into the stumps. Back-to-back yorkers from the left-arm seamer to bowl Sri Lanka Under-19 out for 204!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the national anthems and we are all set for the action to start. Not a single cloud in the sky and it is a bright and sunny morning in Kimberley as the two umpires make their way out to the centre. Matthew Schonken and his boys stride out to the middle and they are joined by the two openers of Sri Lanka Under-19. It will be Pulindu Perera to open the innings alongside Vishen Halambage. Kohl Eksteen will start with the new ball for Zimbabwe Under-19. A slip in place. Here we go...

The first ball in this Group C clash is moments away but before that, the match officials and the two sets of players along with their mascots will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Zimbabwe first followed by Sri Lanka's national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo is pitchside. He says there are no clouds in the sky and the conditions are perfect for a game of cricket with a light breeze which will keep the conditions cool. He then says the square on the west side is the shortest and measures 59 meters and the bowers will have to think where and how to bowl with their captains. Adds that straight back behind the bowler's head is 79 meters and 80 meters on the square on the other end which is a much bigger boundary. Scott Styris says that bowling first is a great decision by Zimbabwe because there is even grass covering but is abrasive and feels that the ball will just stick a bit both for the spinners and seamers. He further says that the first 10 overs will be crucial for the Sri Lankan batters and they will have to play well.

The captain of Sri Lanka Under-19, Sineth Jayawardene says that they were looking to bat first so they got what they wanted. Mentions that they are ready to go. Ends by saying that they are a good team and they are going with three pacers and three spinners.

The skipper of Zimbabwe Under-19, Matthew Schonken says that they will bowl first. Reckons that the pitch might help the seamers early on and would harden out a bit later which is why they have decided to bowl first. He then says this Zimbabwe side has a good mix of seamers and spinners and is looking forward to the game. He concludes that he has always looked to be in this position and is proud to lead the side.

We are at the Diamond Oval in Kimberley, where Group C action in the 2024 Under-19 World Cup will get underway as Sri Lanka Under-19 lock horns with Zimbabwe Under-19. Australia and Namibia are the other two teams in the group, with the two teams at the end of the group stage qualifying for the Super Six stage. Neither Sri Lanka nor Zimbabwe have managed to lift the silverware in their Men's Under-19 World Cup history and will take the field in the quest for their first-ever title. Sri Lanka Under-19 are coming off a shock exit in the 2023 Under-19 Asia Cup, where they failed to make it out of their group featuring Pakistan, the United Arab Emirates, and Japan. Sineth Jayawardene and his boys will have to put that performance behind them as they look to start afresh here in South Africa. In the lead-up to the event, Sri Lanka registered a comprehensive victory against Bangladesh in the first warm-up game before India gave them a taste of their own medicine in the next match. In the batting department, a lot will rest on the young shoulders of skipper Jayawardene, and he will be hoping for support from Dinura Kalupahana and Pulindu Perera. They will heavily rely on Malsha Tharupathi for his leg spin and his handy contributions with the bat lower down the order. Other than Tharupathi, Vishen Halambage and Rusanda Gamage will be looked upon as the all-rounder options from Sri Lanka. Garuka Sanketh will lead the charge of their pace attack, which also consists of Vishen Halambage as the second frontline seamer. On the other hand, Zimbabwe Under-19 are riding high on confidence after wins over the USA and Ireland in their official warm-up fixtures. Even though the wins have come against inexperienced teams, the young Chevrons will be looking to take that momentum into the main event. Skipper Matthew Schonken will hold the key in the spin department, where he will be complemented by Ryan Kamwemba. They have a good bunch of seamers, with Anesu Kamuriwo, Newman Nyamhuri, and Mashford Shungu in their ranks. Opener and wicketkeeper batter Ryan Kamwemba packs a punch in their batting unit, as do Panashe Taruvinga and Campbell Macmillan.
